passage:
Sumit had rehearsed the apology for two years: long, full of reasons about the new job, the wedding, the flat. Standing at a Mumbai bus stop on Sunday, he saw a poster for the college reunion and thought of Urmila, who had once sat with him through a night of exam panic and whom he had last messaged eighteen months ago. His stomach knotted.

He deleted the long draft. Instead he typed: "Hi Urmila. I miss you, and I'm sorry I went quiet. No excuses. Coffee sometime?" He sent it before he could change his mind.

The reply came that evening: "I missed you too. Saturday?" At the cafe Sumit didn't recite reasons. Urmila teased him about being awful at messages. They agreed on a call every second Sunday. It was small, and it was steady.

qa.q: How long ago did Sumit last message Urmila?
qa.a: Sumit last messaged Urmila eighteen months ago.

qa.q: Why did Sumit delete the long draft?
qa.a: Sumit felt nervous, his stomach knotted, and seems to have sensed that a long list of reasons would sound like excuses, so he chose a short honest message.

qa.q: What made Sumit's approach to repair work?
qa.a: A short honest message with no excuses, followed by a small steady plan: a call every second Sunday.

qa.q: How might Urmila have felt on receiving the message?
qa.a: Urmila's reply, 'I missed you too', suggests Urmila was glad and had been missing Sumit as well.

grounding: Sumit lets a friend slip because of work and marriage, feels guilty, and repairs with a short honest message and a small consistent plan.

passage:
Madhuri: Eshaan. I don't even know how to start this
Madhuri: I've been a terrible friend for two years. Missed your birthday twice. Missed your dad's retirement party.
Madhuri: no excuse, work and the wedding just ate me. but I miss you. and I'm sorry.

(Three hours later)
Eshaan: wow. hi
Eshaan: I'm not going to lie, it hurt. I stopped inviting you after a while
Madhuri: that's fair. I deserved that 😔
Eshaan: I did miss you though
Madhuri: can I call you Saturday? even ten minutes
Eshaan: ok. Saturday

(Saturday)
Madhuri: calling in 5?
Eshaan: yes 🙂

(The next Saturday)
Madhuri: same time?
Eshaan: you're actually doing this huh
Madhuri: every Saturday. small and boring and consistent 😄
Eshaan: I'll take boring

qa.q: How many of Eshaan's birthdays did Madhuri miss?
What was Madhuri feeling as she wrote her first messages?
qa.a: Madhuri felt guilty and nervous, admitting to being a terrible friend and not knowing how to start.

qa.q: Why did Madhuri's approach help repair the friendship?
qa.a: Madhuri kept it short and honest without long excuses, then followed up with small, regular Saturday calls.

qa.q: How did Eshaan feel when Madhuri reached out?
qa.a: Eshaan was hurt and a bit guarded at first, admitting to giving up on invitations, but had missed Madhuri too.

grounding: A chat shows a young adult who let a good friend slip away through busy work and marriage, and who sends a short honest apology and starts small, consistent repair.

passage:
Every Pongal, Shalini went home to her village near Thanjavur, and every year she avoided the lane where Vasudha lived. Vasudha had written to her, called her, even sent a wedding card three years ago. Shalini, buried in her Chennai job and her own marriage, had never gone. She'd sent nothing, not even a message.

This year, buying jaggery at the corner shop, she turned and there was Vasudha, holding a toddler on her hip.

Shalini's face went hot. A dozen excuses rose: the office, the traffic, the in-laws. She swallowed them.

"Vasu. I've missed you. I'm sorry I disappeared. I have no good reason."

Vasudha looked at her for a long moment. "I stopped expecting you." Then her face softened slightly. "This is Kavin."

Shalini knelt and shook the boy's fat hand. That night she sent Vasudha a photo of the kolam she'd drawn. The next Sunday, from Chennai, she sent another.

qa.q: What was Shalini buying at the corner shop?
How did Shalini feel when she saw Vasudha?
qa.a: Shalini felt guilty and embarrassed, her face hot, with many excuses rising up.

qa.q: Why was Shalini's short apology the right choice?
qa.a: Swallowing the excuses and saying simply that she missed Vasudha and was sorry was honest, and small regular messages afterwards began real repair.

qa.q: How does Vasudha feel meeting Shalini again?
qa.a: Vasudha feels hurt and guarded, having stopped expecting her, but she softens a little by introducing her son.

grounding: The passage shows a young woman who let a good friend slip away due to work and marriage, who offers a short honest apology instead of excuses and begins small, steady repair.
